newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Gold/silver mining rally seen near end.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Gold/silver mining rally seen near end.

text.p: The rally in precious metals mining companies is likely near its end after three straight weeks of glittering gains, technical analysts said on Monday.

The recent run on precious metals and the companies that mine them has had some on Wall Street wondering if investors were poised to abandon equities. Since early February, blue chips have run in place and tech stocks have faltered.

In contrast, mining stocks, as measured by the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Gold and Silver Index, surged about 14 percent between February 11, when the index closed at 107.37 and February 28, when it closed at 122.46.
Over the same period, the April COMEX gold contract GCJ7 has jumped 6.7 percent to about $365 per ounce from $342.
Today, the index gave back some ground, falling 2.35 points or 1.92 percent to 120.11 after opening at its 200-day moving average of 121.72. April gold dipped $1.10 to $364.00.
Technicians said the gold rally appears spent and does not signal a broad downturn for equities.
"This is a game people play about once every nine months," said Alfred Goldman, technical analyst at A.G. Edwards and Sons. "And I think the game is basically over for another six to nine months."
"I would avoid gold, period. It's up for the wrong reasons," he said. "We don't have an inflation problem and we don't have a world war problem."
Analysts said interest in the mining group seemed more to reflect short-term investor disaffection with the broad market than a broad shift to the sector, a traditional haven during unstable times.
For now, they said, the charts do not support a bullish read on the group.

"The chart pattern in the XAU I would read as having moved from negative to neutral," said Gregory A. Nie, technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "Yes, you are bouncing up from the low, but you still have work to do to really get a look on the chart pattern that's intermediate bullish."
Technicians said key resistance for the index lies ahead at the 130 level and a break above there would warrant a new look.
But few, if any, are counting on the index getting even that far, because the fundamental problems that have dogged gold remain in place.

"Gold has rallied here in part because of some profit-taking finally in the dollar, but the dollar trend to me still seems to be very much intact in the longer term," said Ed Nicoski, technical analyst at Piper Jaffray.
"What you're basically seeing here in gold and gold stocks is a bear market rally," he said. "I don't think it has major implications for the overall market."
